title: Twitter from scratch
description: Post tweets, follow users, read a home timeline. Built up step by step.

steps.title: Requirements and clients
steps.summary: 500M users, 200M daily active. Reads outnumber writes about 100 to 1, so the read path drives the design.

steps.title: Edge: DNS, CDN, WAF, API gateway
steps.summary: Every request enters through one guarded door. Static media never reaches our servers.

steps.title: Core services and their databases
steps.summary: Split users and tweets into services that own their data.

steps.title: Media storage
steps.summary: Images and videos go to object storage and are served through the CDN.

steps.title: Home timeline with fan-out
steps.summary: Precompute each user's timeline when a tweet is posted, so reading it is one cache lookup.

steps.title: Search
steps.summary: A separate search index fed by the same tweet events.

notes.text: Read heavy: ~100 timeline reads for every tweet posted. Optimise reads first.
Blocks bots, scraping and injection before they cost us compute.
Celebrities (>1M followers) skip fan-out. Their tweets are merged in at read time.

decisions.title: One API gateway in front of all services
decisions.why: Auth, rate limiting and routing live in one place instead of in every service.
decisions.tradeoffs: An extra hop and a component that must scale with all traffic.

decisions.title: Cassandra for tweets
decisions.why: Tweets are write-heavy, append-only and read by (user, time). Cassandra partitions that natively and scales by adding nodes.
decisions.tradeoffs: No joins or ad-hoc queries; data is modelled per query.

decisions.title: Fan-out on write into Redis
decisions.why: Building a timeline at read time means querying hundreds of followees per request. Precomputing makes the hot path one cache read.
decisions.tradeoffs: Writes cost O(followers) and timelines take memory; hence the celebrity exception.

decisions.title: Separate search index fed by events
decisions.why: Full-text search does not fit Cassandra. Indexing from the event stream keeps the tweet write path fast.
alternatives: Search directly in the primary database
decisions.tradeoffs: Search results are eventually consistent, a few seconds behind.
